{"body":"## Problem

On the Results view's **Pipeline runs** tab, the "Failure reason" column (`frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx`, the `columns: ColumnsType<PipelineRun>` array around the `failure_reason` entry) has no `width` and no `ellipsis`. `pipeline_runs.failure_reason` is `String(2048)` on the backend (`backend/app/db/models.py`) — a real provider error string (ADF/Airflow) can be very long. With no bound, a long value stretches the whole column (and the table's horizontal scrollbar with it) to fit the entire string on one line, making the scrollbar unusably long and the table hard to use.

## Fix

Give the column a bounded fixed width with single-line ellipsis, and reveal the full text on hover — the standard antd pattern: `width: <px>` + `ellipsis: { showTitle: false }` on the column, with the cell's `render` wrapped in a `<Tooltip title={fullText}>` (custom tooltip since `showTitle: false` suppresses antd's own native-title one). Keep the existing `'—'` null placeholder un-tooltipped.

## Scope

1. Primary: the pipeline-runs "Failure reason" column.
2. Audit every other antd `Table` (`ColumnsType` definitions) across `frontend/src` for columns rendering unbounded free text (error/reason/message/description-like content) and apply the same treatment where warranted. Columns that are already bounded (tags, timestamps, fixed-vocabulary status, names capped at input) are out of scope.","closedAt":"2026-08-08T05:58:14Z","number":1184,"state":"CLOSED","title":"Pipeline-runs Failure-reason column is unbounded — long errors stretch the table (apply fixed-width ellipsis to long-text columns)"}

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ && cat > /tmp/issue_body.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

The bounded-width + ellipsis + tooltip pattern shipped by #1185 (pipeline-runs "Failure reason", `ellipsisColumn`, width 260) and #1208 (run-detail "Observed", width 220) **has never actually worked at runtime, in any environment.** Both are present in the deployed prod bundle and both render unbounded. User-reported against live prod 2026-08-09.

This is not a stale deploy — verified by downloading the live prod chunks:
- `assets/Results-fEYNaYRi.js` → `Y('Failure reason','failure_reason',260)`
- `assets/RunDetail-8_xBzFNQ.js` → `{title:'Observed',dataIndex:'observed_value',width:220,ellipsis:{showTitle:!1},…}`

## Root cause

Every DataQ table renders with `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`. rc-table turns that into `style="width: max-content; min-width: 100%"` on the `<table>` element (`@rc-component/table/es/Table.js:265`). A CSS intrinsic-sizing keyword makes the browser size the table from its **content**, which neuters `table-layout: fixed` — the `<colgroup><col style="width:260px">` becomes a non-binding hint, the cell grows to fit the whole string on one line, and `text-overflow: ellipsis` never triggers because nothing overflows.

So `width` + `ellipsis: { showTitle: false }` on a column are **inert in a `max-content` table**. rc-table even carries a comment about the interaction (ant-design/ant-design#25227).

Measured on the real component (local stack, Chromium, pipeline-runs table with a realistic ADF error injected into a cell):

| | value |
|---|---|
| declared col width | `260px` |
| rendered cell width | **1917px** |
| ellipsis showing | **false** |
| computed `table-layout` | `fixed` |
| computed table `width` | `max-content` |

Isolated CSS repro (same three columns, same long payload, 800px container):

| table style | Observed col rendered | clipped |
|---|---|---|
| `table-layout:fixed; width:max-content` | 1479px | **no** |
| `table-layout:fixed; width:100%` | 409px | yes |
| `table-layout:auto; width:max-content` | 1479px | no |

## Why the tests passed

`frontend/tests/pages/RunDetail.test.tsx:799` asserts `expect(trigger.closest('td')).toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — i.e. that antd *applied the class*. jsdom performs no layout, so no jsdom test can observe that the class has no effect. Same shape as the recurring lesson in CLAUDE.md §13: a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing.

## Scope

All 14 tables in `frontend/src` use `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, so this is systemic, not specific to two columns — any future column-level `ellipsis` will be inert too. Currently affected:

1. `src/components/shared/ellipsisColumn.tsx` (used by `src/pages/Results.tsx:534`)
2. `src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:493-507` (Observed)

You're not missing anything — my claim was wrong. The fix is deployed and it doesn't work.

## What I verified

**Not a stale deploy.** I pulled the live prod chunks off `dataq-app-frontend`:
- `assets/Results-fEYNaYRi.js` → `Y('Failure reason','failure_reason',260)`
- `assets/RunDetail-8_xBzFNQ.js` → `{title:'Observed',dataIndex:'observed_value',width:220,ellipsis:{showTitle:!1},…}`

Both #1185's and #1208's code is in the bundle you're looking at.

**The pattern itself is inert.** Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into `style="width: max-content"` on the `<table>` ([`@rc-component/table/es/Table.js:265`](frontend/node_modules)). An intrinsic-sizing keyword makes the browser size the table from its *content*, which neuters `table-layout: fixed` — the `<col style="width:260px">` becomes a non-binding hint, the cell grows to fit the whole string, and `text-overflow: ellipsis` never fires because nothing overflows.

Measured on the real pipeline-runs table in the local stack, with a realistic ADF error in the cell:

| declared col width | rendered cell width | ellipsis showing |
|---|---|---|
| 260px | **1917px** | **no** |

Isolated CSS repro confirms the mechanism: `fixed`+`max-content` → 1479px unclipped; `fixed`+`100%` → 409px clipped.

**Why the tests passed.** [RunDetail.test.tsx:799](frontend/tests/pages/RunDetail.test.tsx#L799) asserts `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — that antd *applied the class*. jsdom does no layout, so no jsdom test can see that the class has no effect. Same shape as the recurring lesson in CLAUDE.md §13.

**Scope is systemic:** all 14 tables in `frontend/src` use `max-content`, so any column-level `ellipsis` is inert. In-cell `Typography.Text ellipsis` without an explicit `maxWidth` (e.g. [Results.tsx:495](frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx#L495)) fails the same way.

Filed as [#1282](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1282) with the measurements and both fix candidates, each verified working on the live component:

- **Option A (recommended):** bound the *inner* element — inline-block with `max-width` + overflow/ellipsis — inside `ellipsisColumn` and RunDetail's Observed render. Measured 260px, clipped ✅. Local, keeps the tooltip, immune to `max-content`.
- **Option B:** swap `scroll={{x:'max-content'}}` for a px total. Also works, but needs a hand-picked width per table across 14 tables.

Correction to the record: CLAUDE.md §13 says #1184's fix "was already live in prod" and #1208 was the missing piece. Both halves are wrong — #1184's fix has been live and inert since it merged. I'll amend that with the fix.

Before saying a fix is applied/deployed/working, double-check two separate things:

1. **Is the code actually in the running artifact?** Not "the PR merged" — pull the deployed thing and grep it. For the frontend: read the FQDN from `az containerapp show -n dataq-app-frontend …`, fetch `/`, follow the hashed `/assets/*.js` chunks (rolldown code-splits per page — the entry chunk is only ~32KB, page code lives in `Results-<hash>.js`, `RunDetail-<hash>.js`, …) and grep for the changed source.
2. **Does it change observed behavior?** A green unit test can assert the *mechanism was configured* and still be blind to whether the mechanism *does anything*. For anything visual, measure in a real browser (Playwright against the local stack) — `getBoundingClientRect().width`, `scrollWidth > clientWidth` — not jsdom, which performs zero layout.

**Why:** on 2026-08-09 I told the user #1184 was fixed and live. It was in the prod bundle and had never worked in any environment: every table uses `scroll={{x:'max-content'}}`, which sets `width:max-content` on the `<table>` and neuters `table-layout:fixed`, so column `width` + `ellipsis` are inert (issue #1282). The covering test asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — true, and meaningless. The user found it by looking at the screen.

**How to apply:** treat "the class/prop/config is present" as step one of two. State what you verified and how, and if you only checked that the code shipped, say only that. Same family as [[feedback_verify_the_reason_not_just_the_result]] and [[feedback_verify_locally_before_push]]; the driver-boundary version is [[dev-otel-exporter-log-loop-starved-celery]]-adjacent — a fixture or a jsdom DOM that encodes our model can't falsify it.

fix(frontend): bound long-text cells on the inner element so the ellipsis actually binds

Fixes #1282

The bounded-width + ellipsis + tooltip pattern from #1185 and #1208 was inert
at runtime and had never worked in any environment. Every table renders
`scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into `width: max-content`
on the `<table>`; a CSS intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its
content, which neuters `table-layout: fixed` and demotes the `<colgroup>` width
to a non-binding hint. The cell then grows to fit the whole string on one line
and `text-overflow: ellipsis` never fires. Measured on the real component: a
260px-declared Failure-reason column rendering at 1917px, table 2969px wide.

Bound the inner element instead — an inline-block with `max-width` caps the
cell's max-content contribution regardless of what the table's own width
resolves to. Applied via a shared `boundedTextStyle` helper to the pipeline-runs
Failure-reason column, the run-detail Observed column, and the Provider-run id
(whose `Typography` `ellipsis` prop was inert for the same reason — and could
not be the fix either, since it would clip the copy button with the text).

Verified in a real browser against the running app, not just in jsdom:
Failure reason 260px/clipped (was 1917px/unclipped), Observed 220px/clipped,
Provider run 150px/clipped, pipeline table 1345px (was 2969px).

jsdom performs no layout, so the previous assertion — that antd applied the
`ant-table-cell-ellipsis` class — was true the entire time the column rendered
unbounded. The unit tests now assert the bounding style is applied (both fail
without the fix, mutation-checked) and the real guard is a new Playwright
measurement in e2e/results.spec.ts, whose locators and thresholds were executed
against the live app. Its third assertion was rewritten after the first version
measured the hidden Runs table at 0px and could not fail.

The demo seed gains a third pipeline run carrying a full-length ADF error:
`failure_reason` is String(2048) and the seeded short reason could not exercise
the bound, which is part of why this stayed invisible.

CLAUDE.md §13's account of the 2026-08-09 deploy is corrected — it recorded
#1184 as already-live-and-working and #1208 as the only missing piece; both
halves were wrong.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Fixes #1282

## What was wrong

The bounded-width + ellipsis + tooltip pattern from #1185 (pipeline-runs "Failure reason") and #1208 (run-detail "Observed") **was inert at runtime and had never worked in any environment.** User-reported against live prod on 2026-08-09, after CLAUDE.md had recorded it as fixed twice.

It is not a stale deploy — both were present in the shipped bundle (`assets/Results-fEYNaYRi.js` → `Y('Failure reason','failure_reason',260)`, `assets/RunDetail-8_xBzFNQ.js` → `width:220,ellipsis:{showTitle:!1}`).

Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`. rc-table turns that into `style="width: max-content"` on the `<table>` (`@rc-component/table/es/Table.js:265`); a CSS intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its content, which neuters `table-layout: fixed` and demotes the `<colgroup>` width to a non-binding hint. The cell grows to fit the whole string on one line and `text-overflow: ellipsis` never fires, because nothing overflows.

## The fix

Bound the **inner** element rather than the column: an inline-block with `max-width` caps the cell's max-content contribution regardless of how the table's own width resolves. Shared as `boundedTextStyle` and applied to three cells — the two above, plus the Provider-run id, whose `Typography` `ellipsis` prop was inert for the same reason (and could not have been the fix either: it would clip the copy button along with the text).

## Measured on the real component, in a browser

| cell | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Failure reason (declared 260px) | 1917px, not clipped | **260px, clipped** |
| Observed (declared 220px) | unbounded | **220px, clipped** (content 1494px) |
| Provider run | unbounded | **150px, clipped**, copy button intact |
| pipeline-runs table | 2969px | **1345px** |

## Why the tests didn't catch it

`RunDetail.test.tsx` asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — that antd *applied the class*. That was true the whole time the column rendered unbounded. jsdom performs no layout, so no Vitest assertion can distinguish a working bound from an inert one.

- The unit tests now assert the bounding style is **applied** (both new assertions were mutation-checked: they fail against the unfixed render).
- The assertion that it **works** is a new Playwright measurement in `e2e/results.spec.ts`, comparing rendered vs. content width. Its locators and thresholds were executed against the live app before push; its third assertion was rewritten after the first version measured the hidden Runs table at 0px and therefore could not fail.
- The demo seed gains a third pipeline run carrying a full-length ADF error — `failure_reason` is `String(2048)` and the seeded short reason could not exercise the bound, which is part of why this stayed invisible.

## Docs

CLAUDE.md §13's account of the 2026-08-09 deploy is corrected: it recorded #1184 as already-live-and-working and #1208 as the only missing piece. Both halves were wrong.

## Verification

- `prettier --check`, `eslint`, `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `pnpm test:coverage` — 961 tests / 92 files pass, 89.71% lines (gate 80)
- backend `black --check` / `ruff` / `mypy` clean on the seed change; `test_demo_seed_incidents.py` passes
- browser-verified on the local stack against real data (numbers above)

## Note

Fixing this in `main` does not fix production — it needs a deploy.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

Scoped to S3-compatible Iceberg backends — DataQ's own Azure prod uses ADLS-backed Iceberg, likely unaffected) and [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation console warnings — `Modal.maskClosable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`, `Drawer.width` — cosmetic, batch-fixable). Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Review found the migrate-job engine (`alembic/env.py`, its own independent engine, exposed to the same gap and test-enforced-parity-tracked per its own docstring) hadn't been mirrored — fixed same-PR with a matching AST regression test; the driver-guard gap was deferred to #1266 above rather than fixed inline, to keep the PR focused. **#1253** (`observed_value` retention sweep): `purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubbed `sample_failures` but never the sibling list-shaped `observed_value` JSONB — correctly redacted on every read since #1252, but persisting indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep. Fixed with a shared `_purge_column` helper reused across both columns. **#1230** (PII classifier evidence-window, option 2 chosen): the #1196 sample cap narrowed the classifier's evidence to 20 rows at capture time for pandas-backed datasources, which can flip a genuinely-PII column to "not PII" on a noisy 20-row window. Fixed by persisting a compact per-column `value_signal_summary` (5 small ints) over the FULL pre-cap population alongside the capped rows, which the classifier prefers when present and validates before trusting (rejects a summary with an inflated/inconsistent sub-count). A `/code-review` round live-verified a real crash — `_valid_summary`'s except clause didn't catch `OverflowError`, so a persisted JSONB summary with a huge float (`"n": 1e400` → `inf`) 500'd the entire read path instead of degrading to "no summary" — and found the summary wasn't threaded into the sibling `partial_unexpected_list`'s redaction (only `unexpected_index_list`'s), leaving a column masked on one list still shown on the other for the same run; both fixed and mutation-checked same-PR. **#1251** (consolidate hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles): five files each hand-rolled a near-identical class implementing the `SecretStore` Protocol, folded into one shared `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py::FakeSecretStore`. The migration surfaced a real bug along the way — FastAPI's dependency-override resolution introspects the override CALLABLE's own signature, so a bare class (not a lambda) with constructor params, even all-defaulted ones, gets those params bound as request-level params and corrupts body validation for the endpoint under test; a bare `_WriteFailStore()` override was making `POST /connections` 422 instead of ever reaching the route. Review found the fix was patched inline at only the two call sites that hit it rather than encoded at the seam — promoted into a shared `override_secret_store(app, store)` helper (documented in the module docstring) in a same-PR follow-up commit, and `test_admin.py`'s pre-existing `_with_store` now delegates to it instead of duplicating the same lambda wrap. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1260) merged, closing [#1226](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1226) — net unchanged, offset by filing [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261). **#1226**: when every alert channel failed, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` logged a full traceback per failing channel and then the caller (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) logged the SAME last-channel traceback a second time via its own bare `except Exception:`. Fixed with a plain marker attribute (`mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` in `alerting/base.py`, the same stash-on-the-object technique already used by `celery_app.py`'s `_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR`) the composite sets on the re-raised error, so both callers downgrade to a warning for an error the composite already reported, while anything the composite never saw still gets a full traceback. Two full `/code-review` rounds (8 agents total) found zero correctness defects — three concrete "could this fail" scenarios (setattr on `__slots__`-based exceptions, marker loss across the `asyncio.to_thread` hop, exception-identity loss via re-wrapping) were each traced and ruled out with evidence, not assumed away — but did surface real polish gaps, all fixed same-PR: the downgraded warning in `main.py` carried zero identifying fields (now carries `error_type`); a comment overstated what `run_poll_staleness_check` does with the exception (it never catches it — corrected); a test file had invented a THIRD near-identical "channel that raises" double instead of reusing the one two files over (deduped); and a `# pragma: no cover` on the except block had gone stale now that both branches are directly tested (removed, verified via a real coverage run that both lines are hit). One idea deliberately deferred rather than acted on: centralizing the downgrade in the structlog processor chain (the CLAUDE.md §10 "redact at the logger, not the call site" precedent) — reasonable for 3+ callers, premature for the 2 that exist today — filed as #1261. (Previous — **29** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone (46 open repo-wide as of 2026-08-09, re-counted with `gh issue list` AFTER PR [#1252](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1252) (closed [#1229](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1229)) and PR [#1255](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1255) (closed [#1254](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1254)) both merged — net unchanged (46), because closing #1229 (-1) was offset by filing [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253) (+1, retention-sweep gap below) and #1254 was filed-then-closed same session (net 0). **#1229** (`results.observed_value` unbounded/unredacted for set-oriented GX expectations, e.g. `expect_column_distinct_values_to_be_in_set` — every distinct value a high-cardinality column ever saw persisted with no cap and no column-redaction, unlike `sample_failures` which #1196 already covered) was fixed by #1252: a capture-time cap (`gx_runner._bounded_observed_value`, reusing `SAMPLE_ROW_CAP`) plus read-time classification/redaction (`run_service.redact_observed_value` gained a `tested_column` param, threaded through the 3 read paths — `GET /runs/{id}`, the alert builder, `/mcp`'s `get_suite_results`) that classifies over the FULL persisted list before capping what's emitted, matching the established `redact_sample_failures` pattern; kept consistent with #1203's already-merged handling of the adjacent `{"error": ...}` branch in the same function. `/code-review`'s 5-agent pass found nothing above the 80-confidence bar — two sub-80 items (a doc overclaim, fixed in-PR; the retention-sweep scope question, filed as #1253 rather than scope-crept in) were still acted on per CLAUDE.md §11. Mutation-checked: reverted just the two source files, confirmed all new tests fail for the right reason, restored the fix. **#1253** (filed, open, `v1.1 Backlog`): `purge_expired_sample_failures` only scrubs `sample_failures`, never `observed_value` — a list-shaped `observed_value` is now correctly redacted on every READ (#1252) but the raw JSONB persists indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep, unlike its sibling column. Deliberately NOT folded into #1252 — the original #1229 issue's own suggested fix shape asked only for the cap + redaction halves. **#1254** (filed AND closed same session, via #1255): CI on #1252 hit a *pre-existing, unrelated* flaky Vitest test — `SuiteForm.test.tsx`'s "reopens an existing batch target in batch mode" test renders a form whose target is `active` from first mount, so the real 400ms preview debounce (#1193) fires; the test never mocked `previewBatchTarget`'s resolution (unlike siblings that do), so when CI load let the timer win the race against RTL's unmount cleanup, the un-implemented `vi.fn()` returned `undefined` and `.then()` on `undefined` threw — `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then') at Timeout._onTimeout SuiteForm.tsx:387:9`. Confirmed unrelated to #1252 (its diff is backend-only) and confirmed NOT a one-off — a first CI retry reproduced the identical failure, ruling out "just a flake, retry past it." Root-caused precisely (two more sibling tests in the same describe block had the identical latent exposure, not just the one that happened to fail) and reproduced deterministically pre-fix via a scratch forced-delay experiment that threw the exact CI error, then fixed all three vulnerable tests by mocking `previewBatchTarget`'s resolution, matching the idiom used elsewhere in the file. Merged as #1255, then merged into #1252's branch so its CI could go green. Both PRs milestoned/labelled after the fact (an oversight caught mid-session — new issues/PRs must get labels+milestone per the repo's GitHub-hygiene convention, not just inherit one from a linked issue). (Previous — **29** in the v1.1 Backlog milestone, 46 open repo-wide, re-counted with `gh issue list` AFTER PR [#1235](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1235) merged rather than predicted from it — net +1, because it closed [#1199](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1199) and filed two: [#1247](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1247) (the near-miss read side re-derives the write side's candidate tuples and hash-probes `workspace_health`, so the two derivations are coupled by a prose comment plus one round-trip test rather than by shared code) and [#1248](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1248) (four of #1193's batch-preview tests fail under `SECRET_STORE=openbao`, the local-stack default since #1159 — reproduced on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so pre-existing, and it costs every contributor a false-alarm triage round). #1199 gave the #1186/#1194 env near-miss signal a read path: it had been write-only, a `workspace_health` row visible only via `psql`. Two `/code-review` rounds caught six defects, and the first was the one that mattered: **`GET /orchestration/near-misses` shipped auth-only**, by analogy to its `/orchestration/pipelines` neighbour. The analogy was wrong — `pipeline_runs` is workspace-wide orchestrator telemetry with no suite-ownership concept, whereas a near-miss is derived *wholly* from `trigger_binding` rows, which are suite-owned config the sibling `GET /trigger-bindings` already scopes. As written, any signed-in user could enumerate the `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, binding_env)` of bindings on suites they cannot see. It now applies the same `accessible_suite_ids` filter, with `include_all` for a workspace admin. Three more were honesty-of-display: the panel picked the FIRST matching near-miss with `.find()`, so a second live mismatch on the same binding — two orchestrator connections reporting one DAG id against two different wrong envs, i.e. literally the #1186 ambiguity the feature exists to catch — was hidden behind the first; a failed near-miss fetch rendered identically to "no mismatch", so an outage read as healthy on the very screen built to surface it (the ADR-0039 lesson, in a new place); and the tooltip asserted the present tense ("runs keep landing in X … this binding has not fired and won't") for anything inside the 48h window while `updated_at` was fetched, typed, threaded through and never rendered — so a binding fixed an hour ago kept being told it was still broken. The last two were process: the tests drove the write LEAF rather than `orchestration_service._record_env_near_misses`, where the hashed tuple is actually *chosen*, so a change there could have desynced read from write and shipped green (a round-trip test through the real write path now covers it); and four new `assert client.get(...)` calls would have been deleted whole by `python -O` — caught by the #787 `test_assert_hygiene` guard, which is exactly what it is for. **CI caught one more that three green local runs did not**: splitting the near-miss resilience assertions into two `it`s failed the shared frontend run with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then')` AFTER all 92 files reported green — a late effect re-invoking the cleared mock. The file's own docstring had documented that exact hazard; the lesson recorded is to check the **exit code**, not the "N passed" line.))))))) |

[#1242](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1242) — the deferred half of #1104 above.
Fixed by PR #1258 (`fix/issue-1242-inventory-zero-table-enumeration`): the design decision left
open by the issue is implemented as the combined option — a persisted zero-table state **plus** a
transition signal, not reporting-only. Two more nullable `connections` columns (migration
`5ffa2405f9e8`, additive, tested up/down/up locally): `inventory_sync_last_table_count` (the row
count from the last SUCCESSFUL sync only — NULL = never synced, 0 = synced but nothing visible,
>0 = synced N tables; a failed attempt leaves it untouched, since it has no count to report) and
`inventory_sync_zero_since` (set only when the count DROPS from a previously-recorded N>0 to 0 —
the privilege-loss/dropped-database signal; held while it stays at 0, cleared on recovery above
0). A connection that has *always* enumerated zero never sets `_zero_since`, so it renders as a
neutral "0 tables found" note on the connections list rather than an error or warning — reusing
`inventory_sync_last_error` for this would just move the #828 "confident wrong answer" failure
mode to the opposite polarity. A genuine drop renders as a distinct "tables dropped to 0" warning
badge, gated on the sync currently NOT failing (so a stale count from before the sync started
erroring can't be read as the current state). `_record_sync_outcome` and `_has_sync_state`/

### Column ellipsis was inert in every table (2026-08-09)

[#1282](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1282) — user-reported against live prod,
after this file and CLAUDE.md had both recorded the underlying defect as fixed. Fixed by PR
[#1283](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1283).

The bounded-width + ellipsis + tooltip pattern shipped by #1185 (pipeline-runs "Failure reason")
and #1208 (run-detail "Observed") **had never worked, in any environment.** Not a stale deploy —
both were confirmed present in the live prod chunks (`Results-fEYNaYRi.js`, `RunDetail-8_xBzFNQ.js`).
Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into
`width: max-content` on the `<table>`; a CSS intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its
content, which **neuters `table-layout: fixed`** and demotes the `<colgroup>` width to a
non-binding hint. Measured on the real component: a 260px-declared column rendering at **1917px**,
table 2969px wide. The fix bounds the **inner element** (`boundedTextStyle`) instead, which caps
the cell's max-content contribution however the table's own width resolves; applied to both
columns plus the Provider-run id, whose `Typography` `ellipsis` prop was inert for the same reason.

**Why three green suites never saw it, and the practice that came out of it.** The covering test
asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — antd *did* apply the class; the class simply
did nothing. jsdom performs no layout, so **no Vitest assertion can distinguish a working bound
from an inert one** — the same "a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing" shape
as #520/#823/#953, in CSS rather than at a driver boundary. The unit tests now assert the bounding
style is applied (both mutation-checked) and the guard that it *works* is a pair of Playwright
measurements in `e2e/results.spec.ts`, comparing rendered vs. content width. Both were run against
the live app before push — which caught two defects in the assertions themselves: one measured the
hidden Runs table at 0px and could not fail, and one resolved to `ScalarValue`'s inline `<code>`
(scrollWidth 0) and would have failed in CI. The demo seed gained a full-length ADF error and a
real connector-error `observed_value`, because the short seeded values could not overflow the
bound. Review also caught that bounding the Provider-run id without a Tooltip left the column
identifying a run *worse* than unbounded (two Airflow runs from one day differ only in the clipped
tail) — fixed in the same PR.

**Standing practice this produced:** "merged" is not "deployed", and "deployed" is not "works".
Before reporting a fix as done, verify it is in the running artifact *and* that observed behavior
changed. CLAUDE.md §13's account of the 2026-08-09 deploy was corrected in the same PR — it had
recorded #1184 as already-live-and-working and #1208 as the only missing piece; both were wrong.

### Pending design decisions

Done and merged. Summary:

## The fix ([#1283](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1283), closes [#1282](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1282))

Option A implemented — bound the **inner element**, not the column. Shared as `boundedTextStyle` in [ellipsisColumn.tsx](frontend/src/components/shared/ellipsisColumn.tsx), applied to three cells:

| cell | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Failure reason (declared 260px) | 1917px, no ellipsis | 260px, clipped |
| Observed (declared 220px) | unbounded | 220px, clipped (content 1494px) |
| Provider run | unbounded | 150px, clipped + tooltip |
| pipeline-runs table | 2969px | 1345px |

All measured in a real browser against the running app, not inferred.

**Review caught three things, all fixed:** I'd clipped the Provider-run id with no hover reveal, which made that column identify a run *worse* than unbounded — two Airflow runs from one day differ only in the clipped tail; the `OBSERVED_COLUMN_WIDTH` export claimed E2E coverage that didn't exist, so the Observed bound now has its own Playwright measurement; and a stale seed-count comment.

**Two of my own test assertions were wrong and running them found it** — one measured the hidden Runs table at 0px and could never fail; one resolved to `ScalarValue`'s inline `<code>` (scrollWidth 0) and would have failed in CI. Both rewritten and re-verified. The unit assertions were mutation-checked (they fail against the unfixed render), and CI's Playwright job ran both new measurements green.

Docs corrected in the same PR: CLAUDE.md §13 said #1184 was "already live in prod" and #1208 was the only missing piece — both halves were wrong. [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) carries the full entry ([#1284](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1284)).

## Memory

Saved as [feedback-verify-a-fix-is-actually-applied](/Users/arijit/.claude/projects/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/memory/feedback_verify_a_fix_is_actually_applied.md): before calling a fix applied, check two separate things — that the code is in the **running artifact** (fetch the deployed chunks and grep, not "the PR merged"), and that **observed behavior changed** (measure in a real browser for anything visual; jsdom does no layout, so `toHaveClass` proves nothing). Indexed in MEMORY.md.

Migrations are additive/backward-compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the workflow runs
`alembic upgrade head` **before** rolling the apps — the running old code
tolerates the new schema. (This is exactly the dev-DB step that, when skipped,
500s the checks endpoint after a schema-adding deploy.)

Use an **immutable** `image_tag` per release — ACA caches a tag at the node, so a
same-tag rebuild won't be re-pulled on a new revision. Push-on-merge is
intentionally **off**; deploys are manual `workflow_dispatch`.

### Pre-deploy checklist

Confirm the change is *ready and green* before you push it to prod:

- [ ] **Everything intended is merged to `main`** and you're deploying that known SHA (blank
  `image_tag` → the immutable commit SHA).
- [ ] **CI is fully green** on that SHA — lint, format, type-check, **all unit + integration
  tests**, the security scans (Bandit / CodeQL / secret-scan / dependency-audit), and the
  frontend E2E. The local verification battery (the same gate) passes too — don't let CI be
  the first feedback loop.
- [ ] **Docs are up to date** for what's shipping — `CLAUDE.md` §13 headline + `docs/progress.md`
  ticked; an **ADR** for any significant decision; the **env-var reference** + this deploy
  guide for any new config; and **user docs** for any new user-facing feature.
- [ ] **DB migrations are safe** — additive/backward-compatible (nullable `ADD COLUMN` / new
  table; no `DROP`/rename/`NOT NULL`-without-default in the same PR as the code that needs
  it), `upgrade` **and** `downgrade` tested locally. The workflow runs `alembic upgrade head`
  **before** rolling the apps, so old code never sees a missing column — you just confirm the
  revision is safe. *Note:* an `ALTER` on a hot table (`runs` / `results` / `pipeline_runs`)
  can block on a live-worker lock and hang the migrate job (#605); recovery + root-cause
  hardening are in [#708](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/708).
- [ ] **Migration-specific pre-deploy steps have been run.** Some revisions need a manual step
  against the live database *before* the migrate job runs, and that step lives in the
  **migration's own docstring** — not here, because it is revision-specific and would rot if
  duplicated. Before deploying, list the revisions that are pending on prod
  (`alembic current` vs `alembic heads`) and read each one's docstring in
  `backend/alembic/versions/` for a **`MANDATORY PRE-DEPLOY`** section; run what it says and
  confirm the result is clean. First instance: **`7d25617cfaf0`** (users nullable
  `aad_object_id` + unique `lower(email)`, #735) requires a duplicate-email audit — if it
  finds duplicates, the index creation fails and the migrate job aborts, so resolve them
  first.
- [ ] **Config + secrets are in place** — the required GitHub env/vars and Key Vault secrets
  (see the [prerequisites](#before-you-deploy-production-prerequisites) above), especially any
  new key this release reads.

### Post-deploy smoke checklist

After the workflow is green, confirm the app is actually **healthy and fully functional** —
don't stop at HTTP 200s. Work top-down:

- [ ] **It's up & reachable** — `GET /healthz` → 200; the SPA root and a deep link load.
- [ ] **A user can sign in** — complete the Azure AD SSO flow end-to-end and land on the
  dashboard as a real user (not just the login screen).
- [ ] **The UI renders correctly** — walk the key pages (Dashboard, Connections, Suites,
  Results, Profile, Admin) and confirm they render with data and **no console / network
  errors**, on **desktop *and* mobile** viewports. (The `ui-tester` agent automates this.)
- [ ] **Every high-level capability works end-to-end** — spot-check the core flows, e.g.:
  add/edit a connection and **test** it; author a check; **trigger a run** and see live
  progress → results → (redacted) failing samples; view dashboard trends; a schedule; an
  alert delivered; the **MCP tools** answer for an AI client. If a release touched a specific
  area, exercise that area harder.
- [ ] **Auth + guards hold** — unauthenticated API and MCP requests are rejected (`401`), and
  no Swagger/OpenAPI content is served publicly: `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json` on the
  public origin return the **SPA's `index.html`** (the frontend nginx catch-all — they are not
  proxied paths since the ADR 0028 §5 cutover, so a `200` with the SPA shell is the expected
  result, NOT Swagger UI or a JSON schema). The API's own prod-docs gate (`ENVIRONMENT=prod`
  → `404`, #170) still applies on its internal ingress, which is unreachable from outside.
- [ ] **Infra rolled cleanly** — api / worker / frontend are on the **deployed tag** (not the
  old image), the migrate job execution is `Succeeded`, Celery beat starts clean (#405/#407)
  and orchestration polling reads Key Vault (#406/#408), and App Insights shows no post-roll
  errors.
- [ ] **Email OTP mailer, if `AUTH_EMAIL_*` is set** — as a workspace admin, `POST
  /api/v1/admin/auth-email/test` (#737) and confirm the test message actually lands in your
  inbox. A non-2xx response names the failing stage in `error.detail.stage` (`connect` / `tls`
  / `auth` / `send`) — cheaper to catch here than at the first real sign-in attempt:
  ```bash
  # $FE from the reachability probes below; $TOKEN from `az account get-access-token
  # --resource api://<api-client-id>` (see Operational notes) for an admin user.
  curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $FE/api/v1/admin/auth-email/test | jq
  ```
- [ ] **(Optional, deeper)** run the live-smoke lane (`frontend/e2e-live/` gated on
  `E2E_LIVE_BASE_URL` + `e2e_smoke.py` `DATAQ_BEARER` mode, #531) and the MCP 4-query protocol
  smoke for an authenticated end-to-end pass.

**Quick reachability + auth probes** (no token — a `401` *is* the pass for an auth-gated
route; everything is the public **frontend** host since the api has no public ingress, ADR
0028 §5):

```bash
FE=https://<your-frontend-fqdn>   # e.g. az containerapp show -n dataq-app-frontend -g dataq-rg \

A runner/adapter exception can carry DSN, credential, or PII fragments — a

So we **never store or surface the raw exception text**. We read it only to
*classify* it into one of a small allowlist of categories and return a **fixed
per-category message**. The full exception still goes to the server log
(`log.exception`) for operators; only the safe, generic reason reaches the API.

The classification is a best-effort heuristic over the exception type + message;
the default is the neutral ``unknown`` message, so a miss is never a leak — it
just reads as "see the logs".
"""

from enum import StrEnum


class FailureCategory(StrEnum):
    CONFIG = "config"
    CONNECTIVITY = "connectivity"
    PERMISSION = "permission"

cat > /tmp/issue_poll.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

An **orchestration** connection whose poll fails reports a **datasource**-shaped reason. Prod right now, on both Airflow connections:

> The connection or run target looks misconfigured — e.g. a missing warehouse or role, or a table/path that does not exist. Check the connection and the suite's run target.

An Airflow connection has no warehouse, no role, no table/path, and no run target. The message sends an operator to check four things that do not exist on the object that failed, and says nothing about the actual cause — the Airflow host is unreachable.

Found during the 2026-08-09 post-deploy smoke of `77068358`. **Pre-existing** — nothing in that deploy touched orchestration.

## Evidence

`GET /api/v1/connections` on prod, 2026-08-10T01:44Z:

| connection | type | last_polled_at | last_poll_error |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apache Airflow | airflow | 01:43:40Z | the CONFIG message above |
| Apache Airflow — QA | airflow | 01:43:38Z | the CONFIG message above |
| Azure Data Factory | adf | 01:43:38Z | — |
| Azure Data Factory — QA | adf | 01:43:39Z | — |
| dbt — Retail Lineage (harness) | dbt | 01:43:40Z | — |

The split is exactly right: ADF is a cloud service and dbt polls an ADLS artifact, so both are reachable; the Airflow host is the harness ACA app, which is `Stopped` by default since 2026-07-04 (#590) — confirmed `dataq-harness-airflow: Stopped`. So the poll *failing* is correct and expected. Only the reason is wrong.

## Root cause — two stacked, either one worth fixing

1. **The message vocabulary is datasource-specific but the classifier is shared.** `backend/app/services/failure_classifier.py` `_MESSAGES[CONFIG]` is written for a failed *run* against a warehouse/file ("warehouse or role", "table/path", "the suite's run target"). `orchestration_service.py:820` reuses it verbatim for a *poll* failure on an ADF/Airflow/dbt connection, where none of those nouns apply. This holds for `PERMISSION` and `CONNECTIVITY` too — both say "the datasource", which an orchestration provider is explicitly not (CLAUDE.md §4).
2. **A dead host classifies as CONFIG, not CONNECTIVITY.** A stopped ACA app answers with a 404-shaped response; `_MARKERS` checks CONNECTIVITY before CONFIG, but none of the connectivity markers (`timed out`, `connection refused`, `unreachable`, `getaddrinfo`, …) match a 404 body, while CONFIG's `not found` does. So "the host is down" is reported as "your configuration is wrong".

The redaction property is intact and must stay intact — the raw exception can carry a DSN or bearer token, so the fix is a better *classification and message set*, never surfacing raw text.

## Suggested fix

Give the classifier a caller-supplied surface (`run` vs `orchestration_poll`) and a parallel orchestration message set that names the right nouns ("the orchestration host could not be reached", "the provider rejected the credentials", "the pipeline/DAG id was not found"). Optionally add HTTP-status-aware markers so a 404/502/503 from a provider host lands in CONNECTIVITY rather than CONFIG.

## Why it matters

This is the [#828](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/828) "confident wrong answer" family again: the UI states something specific and wrong with no signal that it is guessing. A silent gap makes you look; a confident misdirection makes you look in the wrong place. It is also the exact failure the ops-log exists to prevent — a stopped Airflow that took two wrong root causes to distinguish from an outage.

def classify_failure_category(exc: BaseException) -> FailureCategory:
    """Best-effort category for a run/dry-run failure. Never raises."""
    haystack = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}".lower()
    for category, markers in _MARKERS:
        if any(marker in haystack for marker in markers):
            return category
    return FailureCategory.UNKNOWN


def classify_failure_reason(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    """The fixed, secret-free user-facing reason for a failed run/dry-run (#605).

    Reads ``exc`` only to pick the category; the returned string is a constant
    from ``_MESSAGES``, so no credential/DSN/PII fragment can ride out on it.
    """
    return _MESSAGES[classify_failure_category(exc)]

def classify_inventory_sync_error(
    exc: BaseException, connection_type: str, *, during_enumeration: bool
) -> str:
    """The fixed, secret-free reason an inventory-sync attempt failed (#1104).

    A missing grant gets a SPECIFIC message naming the system schema the sync
    reads — this is the #828 shape the issue exists to close: toggle on,
    connection test green (the `SELECT 1` probe never exercises this query),
    zero assets ever appear, no surface says why. Every other failure category
    (connectivity/config/unknown) falls back to the generic
    :func:`classify_failure_reason` message, unchanged.

    ``during_enumeration`` is REQUIRED, and is the phase the failure actually
    happened in — ``True`` only once the warehouse connection is open and the
    enumeration query itself is running (`InventorySyncEnumerationError` in
    `inventory_service`). The category markers are broad substrings, so a
    failure that never reached the warehouse at all — a sealed vault or a 403
    from the secret store while resolving the credential, an IdP rejecting the
    token during the driver handshake — matches PERMISSION just as readily as a
    missing `SELECT`. Naming a warehouse grant for one of those sends an admin
    to fix a privilege that was never the problem while the real fault stays
    undiagnosed, which is a *worse* failure than the generic message: a
    confident wrong answer, the exact #828 shape this feature exists to end.
    Phase is the one thing we know for certain, so it gates the specific claim;
    everything else falls back to the hedged generic reason.
    """
    category = classify_failure_category(exc)
    if during_enumeration and category is FailureCategory.PERMISSION:
        schema = _INVENTORY_SCHEMA_BY_TYPE.get(connection_type)
        if schema:
            # Phase narrows this to "the warehouse rejected OUR query", which is as
            # far as the evidence goes: a Snowflake role that lost USAGE on its
            # warehouse is rejected here too, and reads identically. So the message
            # names the most likely cause and the two other privileges worth
            # checking, rather than asserting one of them.
            return (
                f"The inventory-sync query against {schema} was rejected — most likely a "
                "missing SELECT grant there, or a role/warehouse privilege the query "
                "needs. Grant SELECT (or ask your workspace admin to) and it will resolve "
                "automatically on the next sync; if the grants are already in place, "
                "re-check the connection's role and credentials."
            )
    return _INVENTORY_MESSAGES.get(category) or classify_failure_reason(exc)

# ── Orchestration-poll classification (#1285) ────────────────────────────────
# Same shape as the inventory-sync case below, in a different place: the generic
# messages are written for a RUN against a datasource, and an orchestration
# connection (ADF / Airflow / dbt) is explicitly NOT a datasource (CLAUDE.md §4).
# It has no warehouse, no role, no table/path and no run target, so `CONFIG`'s
# "e.g. a missing warehouse or role … check the suite's run target" names four
# things that do not exist on the object that failed, and `CONNECTIVITY` /
# `PERMISSION` both say "the datasource".
#
# This was live in prod: both Airflow connections reported the CONFIG message
# while the actual cause was the harness Airflow app being Stopped. A silent gap
# makes an operator look; a confident misdirection makes them look in the wrong
# place — the #828 shape.
#
# CONFIG deliberately names BOTH plausible causes rather than picking one. A
# stopped host and a deleted DAG are genuinely indistinguishable here: the poll
# is an httpx call ending in `raise_for_status()`, and Container Apps answers for
# a stopped app with the same 404 shape as a real "DAG not found".
_ORCHESTRATION_MESSAGES: dict[FailureCategory, str] = {
    FailureCategory.CONFIG: (
        "The orchestration host answered, but not with what DataQ asked for — either the "
        "pipeline/DAG no longer exists, or the connection's base URL points somewhere "
        "that isn't this provider (a stopped host can look the same). Check the "
        "connection's URL and the pipeline/DAG id on its trigger bindings."
    ),
    FailureCategory.CONNECTIVITY: (
        "The orchestration host could not be reached (network, DNS, TLS, a timeout, or "
        "the host is down). Check that the provider is running and reachable from DataQ."
    ),
    FailureCategory.PERMISSION: (
        "The orchestration provider rejected the credentials, or the identity is missing a "
        "permission it needs to list runs. Re-check the connection's credentials and its "
        "access to the pipelines/DAGs."
    ),
    FailureCategory.UNKNOWN: (
        "Polling this orchestration connection failed for a reason DataQ could not "
        "classify. Re-test the connection, and check the worker logs for the underlying "
        "error."
    ),
}


def classify_orchestration_poll_reason(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    """The fixed, secret-free reason an orchestration poll failed (#1285).

    Same redaction contract as :func:`classify_failure_reason` — ``exc`` is read
    only to pick a category, and the returned string is a constant — but the
    text names orchestration nouns instead of datasource ones.
    """
    return _ORCHESTRATION_MESSAGES[classify_failure_category(exc)]

Fixes #1285

An orchestration connection is not a datasource (CLAUDE.md §4), but its poll
failures were classified through the run-flavoured message set. Live in prod:
both Airflow connections read "The connection or run target looks misconfigured
— e.g. a missing warehouse or role, or a table/path that does not exist. Check
the connection and the suite's run target" while the actual cause was the
harness Airflow app being Stopped. An Airflow connection has no warehouse, no
role, no table/path and no run target — four nouns that don't exist on the
object that failed, and nothing about what did.

Adds `classify_orchestration_poll_reason` with a parallel message set that names
orchestration nouns, and points `record_poll_failure` at it. Same redaction
contract as the run path: the exception is read only to pick a category and the
returned string is a constant, so no DSN or bearer token can ride out. This
mirrors the `classify_inventory_sync_error` precedent (#1104), which solved the
identical problem for inventory sync and left this caller behind.

one: the poll is an httpx call ending in raise_for_status(), and Container Apps
answers for a stopped app with the same 404 shape as a genuine "DAG not found",
so the two are not distinguishable here. Asserting either would just move the
confident-wrong-answer to a new polarity.

the "not found" marker. 404 deliberately stays in CONFIG for the reason above.

An orchestration connection is not a datasource (CLAUDE.md §4), but its poll failures were classified through the run-flavoured message set. Live in prod, both Airflow connections read:

An Airflow connection has no warehouse, no role, no table/path and no run target. The message names four things that don't exist on the object that failed, and says nothing about what did — the harness Airflow app was `Stopped`. That's the [#828](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/828) confident-wrong-answer shape: a silent gap makes you look, a confident misdirection makes you look in the wrong place.

Evidence at 01:44Z — the split is exactly right, only the reason is wrong:

| connection | polled | error |
|---|---|---|
| Apache Airflow ×2 | ✅ | the CONFIG message above |
| Azure Data Factory ×2 | ✅ | — |
| dbt — Retail Lineage | ✅ | — |

ADF is a cloud service and dbt polls an ADLS artifact, so both are reachable; only the Airflow host is stopped.

### Post-deploy smoke findings, 2026-08-09 (`77068358`)

Both found by running the post-deploy checklist against live prod rather than stopping at
HTTP 200s, and both fixed the same day.

**[#1286](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1286) — the fix's own regression.**
PR [#1287](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1287). Bounding the Provider-run id at
150px in a 200px cell left too little room for the copy button, which wrapped to a second line
and grew every pipeline-runs row from 56px to 77px — on the page #1283 had just fixed. Measured
the wrap threshold on live prod across 100–150px (wraps at ≥140, clean at ≤130) and shipped 120
for margin. Review then caught that the new no-wrap assertion **passed against the unfixed
bound**: the seeded run ids were ~17 chars and a `max-width` only ever clips, so the button never
wrapped at any bound. The Airflow seed now carries a real full-length `manual__<iso8601>` id, and
the test asserts `idClipped: true` alongside `copyWrapped: false` — so if the seed ever reverts to
a tidy id the test *fails* rather than silently going inert. That is the same
fixture-too-weak-to-express-the-failure shape as #1282 itself, caught one layer up.

**[#1285](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1285) — orchestration poll failures spoke
datasource.** PR [#1288](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1288). Pre-existing. Both
prod Airflow connections reported "a missing warehouse or role, or a table/path that does not
exist — check the suite's run target" while the real cause was the harness Airflow app being
`Stopped`. An orchestration connection (CLAUDE.md §4) has none of those four things: the message
named only nonexistent nouns and said nothing about what actually failed — the #828
confident-wrong-answer shape. Fixed with `classify_orchestration_poll_reason`, a parallel message
set under the same redaction contract, mirroring the `classify_inventory_sync_error` precedent
(#1104) that had solved this for inventory sync and left this caller behind. CONFIG names **both**
plausible causes rather than picking one, because Container Apps answers for a stopped app with
the same 404 shape as a genuine "DAG not found".

Two review findings on that PR were each worse than the bug being fixed, and are worth carrying:
bare `"502"/"503"/"504"` markers went into the **shared** `_MARKERS` table ahead of CONFIG, so a
sealed OpenBao (`HTTP 503 — vault sealed`) would have been reported as "the datasource could not be
reached" — reintroducing the exact ADR-0039 lesson that an outage must never be reportable as a
benign state; and the new "orchestration" messages were themselves **Airflow-shaped** ("base URL",
"the host answered"), which is the same defect one provider over, since ADF has no base URL and dbt
contacts no host at all. The wiring test even used a dbt connection while asserting Airflow wording
— the test agreed with the author instead of checking them. Markers are now reason phrases only,
messages are provider-neutral, and both properties are pinned across every category.

content.text:
Done. Prod is on `eba60b4d` with everything verified.

## What shipped

Two deploys, both with full pre/post checklists:

| | [run 31347217502](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31347217502) → `77068358` | [run 31350288817](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31350288817) → `eba60b4d` |
|---|---|---|
| carried | #1283 (the ellipsis fix) | #1287 (#1286), #1288 (#1285) |
| migrate | no-op, 0 migration files | no-op, 0 migration files |
| smoke | green | green |

**Pre-deploy** both times: merged SHA, CI green, docs current, zero migrations (single head `5ffa2405f9e8`), no new config keys.

**Post-deploy** both times: healthz/SPA/deep-link 200 · `/api` + `/mcp` 401 (not 421) · openapi 404 · `/docs` = SPA shell · all three apps on the deployed tag · beat + watchdog clean · **zero** error-level lines on the new revisions · 8 pages render with no console or HTTP errors · mobile 390px with no horizontal body scroll · a live Snowflake suite run on each revision.

## Your original complaint, measured in prod

The exact ADF error from your screenshot: **3423px of content now rendering at 260px, clipped.** Observed 220px clipped, pipeline table 1379px instead of 2969px.

## Two things the smoke caught

**[#1286](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1286)** — my own regression. The 150px bound wrapped the copy button, growing every row 56px→77px. Measured the threshold on live prod (wraps ≥140, clean ≤130), shipped 120. Now 20/20 cells clipped, uniform 56px.

**[#1285](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1285)** — pre-existing. Both Airflow connections said *"missing warehouse or role… check the suite's run target"* while the harness Airflow was simply `Stopped`. An orchestration connection has none of those four things. Fixed; the 02:51Z poll wrote the new provider-neutral reason.

Review on that one found two problems **worse** than the bug: my bare `"503"` marker went into the *shared* table and would have reported a sealed OpenBao as "the datasource could not be reached", and my "provider-neutral" messages were themselves Airflow-shaped — with the wiring test using a dbt connection while asserting Airflow wording, so it agreed with me instead of checking me. Both fixed and pinned.

## On verification

Two moments nearly produced another wrong answer, and both are why I didn't stop early:

- Grepping the deployed `Results`/`RunDetail` chunks found nothing — rollup had split `boundedTextStyle` into its own shared chunk. Concluding "not deployed" there would have been wrong.
- The first poll after the roll still showed the old message. I pulled and inspected the deployed image to confirm the code was there, then waited for the next cycle — the draining revision had served that poll.

Also caught three of my own tests that couldn't fail: one measured a hidden table at 0px, one resolved to the wrong element, one passed against the unfixed bound because the seed ids were too short. All fixed so they fail for the right reason.

Recorded in [CLAUDE.md §13](CLAUDE.md), [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md), and memory. Snapshot unmoved at 45 open / 28 backlog / 0 PRs.
